lines.cap: **Narrator:** This is Kavya. She is twelve. It is Saturday, 34 °C, and the aircon has been on since breakfast.
**Mum:** Kavya! Switch off the aircon! You're using up all the energy!
**Kavya:** Actually, Mum, energy can't be used up. It can't be destroyed. We learnt it in science.
**Narrator:** Kavya is half right. So is her mum. Neither of them will admit it.
**Narrator:** But this documentary is not about Kavya. It is about the electricity meter outside her front door.
**Narrator:** Inside is a tiny accounting firm. Its job: to account for every joule that comes through the door.
**Constance:** Constance. Senior auditor. I am the **law of conservation of energy**.
**Constance:** Energy cannot be **created** or **destroyed**. It can only be **transferred** from one store to another.
**Constance:** I have never been broken. Not once in 13.8 billion years. And people have tried.
**Constance:** Now somebody says energy is being '**used up**'. Not on my watch. I'm opening a case.
**Narrator:** Every Joule Counts. Episode 14: The Case of the Missing Joules.
**Narrator:** Case file one. Constance questions her only witness.
**Jules:** Hi hi hi! I'm Jules! I'm a **joule**! Energy is measured in **joules**, J for short!
**Constance:** A joule is tiny. Lifting a small apple up by one metre takes about one joule.
**Jules:** I lifted an apple once! A whole metre! Best day of my life.
**Constance:** So we usually count in **kilojoules**. **1 kJ = 1000 J**.
**Jules:** A banana holds about four hundred thousand of us. It's a very crowded banana.
**Narrator:** Every joule is always in one of **eight stores**. The firm has a department for each.
**Constance:** The tour. Keep up, Jules.
**Constance:** **Kinetic**: anything **moving**. **Gravitational potential**: anything **high up**.
**Jules:** That's Gerald, on the top shelf. He's got a lot of potential.
**Constance:** **Elastic potential**: stretched or squashed things. **Chemical**: food, fuels and batteries.
**Constance:** **Thermal**: warm things, with jiggling particles. **Nuclear**: energy in the **nucleus** of an atom.
**Constance:** **Electrostatic**: charges that attract or repel. And **magnetic**: magnets that attract or repel.
**Jules:** **K**ind **G**orillas **E**at **C**hocolate, **T**igers **N**ever **E**at **M**ango!
**Constance:** Jules made that up. He's very proud of it. He's told the gorillas.
**Kavya:** Hang on. Where's the electricity department? Or light? Or heat?
**Constance:** Not stores.
**Narrator:** Energy moves between stores along **transfer pathways**. In this firm, that means Pat.
**Pat:** Pat. Courier. I don't **keep** energy. I **move** it. Big difference.
**Constance:** Pat is a pathway. People keep trying to file things with Pat. Pat hates that.
**Pat:** Four routes. One: **mechanically**. A **force** pushes, pulls or stretches something.
**Pat:** Kick a ball: I carry energy mechanically into its **kinetic** store.
**Pat:** Two: **electrically**. An **electric current** in a circuit. Like charging your phone.
**Pat:** Three: **by heating**. From a **hotter** thing to a **colder** thing. Hot pan, cold egg.
**Pat:** Four: **by radiation**. Carried by **waves**: light, infrared, sound. Sunshine. Your speaker.
**Jules:** Hey, Pat! Can I leave this light energy with you for a bit?
**Pat:** I'm. Not. A. Store.
**Constance:** **Stores** are **where** energy is held. **Pathways** are **how** it moves. **Heat, light, sound** and **electricity** are pathways.
**Narrator:** Example: Kavya's dad is boiling the kettle for his kopi. At thirty-four degrees. He does not care.
**Pat:** First I go **electrically**, from the mains to the **heating element**.
**Pat:** Then **by heating**, from the element into the water's **thermal store**.
**Kavya:** So that's electrically, then by heating. Two pathways, one kettle.
**Constance:** Correct. Annoyingly.
**Kavya:** She said I was correct. I'm telling everyone.
**Narrator:** Four p.m. A tragedy.
**Narrator:** Kavya's bubble tea is on the edge of the table. Her elbow is about to make a terrible decision.
**Constance:** Before it falls, the cup has energy in its **gravitational potential** store. Because it's **high up**.
**Jules:** It's falling! Gravitational store emptying! **Kinetic** store filling! It's speeding up!
**Kavya:** No no no no no!
**Constance:** Just before it lands, nearly all of it is **kinetic**. Then: splat.
**Theo:** And then it all comes down to me. Hello. Theo. **Thermal store**.
**Theo:** Some went off as **sound**. The rest warmed the floor, the tea and the pearls. A tiny bit.
**Constance:** The **total energy before** equals the **total energy after**. Every joule. I counted.
**Constance:** We file it as an **energy flow diagram**: **gravitational potential → kinetic → thermal + sound**.
**Jules:** Same with a wind-up toy! **Elastic** store in the spring, to **kinetic**, plus a bit of **thermal** from friction!
**Kavya:** I don't care about the joules. I care about my pearls.
**Constance:** The pearls are fine. Energetically speaking.
**Narrator:** Five p.m. The aircon is finally off. Kavya has switched to an old fan. It rattles.
**Constance:** Energy that goes where we **want** is **useful**. For a fan, that's the **kinetic** store of the moving air.
**Constance:** Energy that goes where we **don't** want is **wasted**. Usually into the **thermal store** of the surroundings.
**Theo:** That's me. The motor gets warm. The rattle is sound, and that ends up as heat too. It all ends up with me.
**Theo:** Nobody comes down here on purpose. They just end up here. Like a lost umbrella.
**Jules:** So the wasted energy just vanishes? Poof?
**Constance:** Denied.
**Constance:** Wasted energy is never destroyed. It **dissipates**: it spreads out into the surroundings, thinner and thinner.
**Theo:** I've got all of it. But it's spread so thin, nobody can collect it and use it again. My legacy: a slightly warmer room.
**Narrator:** Waste often comes from **friction** and **air resistance**, transferring energy to **thermal** stores. That's why bike brakes get hot.
**Narrator:** Try it. Rub your palms together fast. Friction transfers energy into the **thermal store** of your skin.
**Kavya:** Ooh. Warm. Okay, that's actually cool.
**Theo:** It's actually warm.
**Narrator:** Every device in the flat gets a yearly review. From Effie.
**Effie:** Effie. **Efficiency**. I measure how much of your energy actually does the job.
**Effie:** I've reviewed every appliance in this flat. The rice cooker cried.
**Effie:** **efficiency = useful energy transferred ÷ total energy supplied**
**Jules:** Useful Over Total! Useful Over Total!
**Effie:** The fan. You were supplied with **200 J**. Only **150 J** went into moving air.
**Effie:** The other **50 J**, **25%**, was wasted. Mostly as heat.
**Theo:** Hello again.
**Effie:** **No** real device is **100%** efficient. There's always some waste, usually heat.
**Jules:** What if I write down a hundred and ten per cent?
**Constance:** Denied. Check your working. You can't get more energy out than you put in.
**Narrator:** Effie's favourite chart: the **Sankey diagram**. Arrow **width** shows the **amount** of energy.
**Effie:** Useful energy carries straight on. Wasted energy **peels off** in a branch, usually downwards.
**Effie:** Fat wasted branch: inefficient. Thin wasted branch: efficient. Simple. Brutal. Beautiful.
**Theo:** I'm the branch. I'm always the branch.
**Narrator:** One question remains: where do the joules come from?
**Colin:** Colin. **Coal**. Three hundred million years underground. I'm a **fossil fuel**.
**Colin:** Me, my brother **Oil**, my cousin **Natural Gas**. Burn us, and the energy in our **chemical store** is released.
**Colin:** In a power station, we heat water into **steam**. The steam spins a **turbine**. The turbine turns a **generator**.
**Constance:** **Chemical → thermal** store of the steam **→ kinetic** store of the turbine. Then **electrically**, down the wires, to here.
**Jules:** Wind and falling water spin turbines directly! Solar cells don't even need a turbine!
**Colin:** I'm **reliable**. Day or night. A little of me releases a lot of energy.
**Constance:** But burning fossil fuels releases **carbon dioxide**, a greenhouse gas linked to **climate change**. And they're **non-renewable**. They'll run out.
**Colin:** Three hundred million years to make me. Twenty minutes to burn me. Nobody respects the process.
**Jules:** What about nuclear? It hardly makes any carbon dioxide. So it's renewable, right?
**Constance:** Denied. Nuclear fuel is **uranium**. It's mined, and it will run out. Nuclear is **non-renewable**.
**Narrator:** **Renewable** resources are constantly replaced, so they won't run out: **solar**, **wind**, **hydroelectric**, **tidal**, **wave**, **geothermal** and **biomass**.
**Jules:** **S**ix **W**ild **H**orses **T**ook **W**et **G**rass **B**ack!
**Constance:** Most release little carbon dioxide. But many are **unreliable**: no solar at night, no wind on a calm day.
**Narrator:** So countries use a **mix**. Singapore gets most of its electricity from **natural gas**, and puts solar panels on HDB roofs.
**Kavya:** So nothing was used up. It was all just... in Theo's basement?
**Constance:** Case closed. No joule was destroyed. But plenty were **wasted**: spread out as heat, doing nothing useful.
**Constance:** **Saving energy** doesn't mean stopping joules vanishing. It means **wasting less** of what we pay for.
**Narrator:** So: **insulate** homes, choose **efficient appliances**, and **switch off** things instead of leaving them on **standby**.
**Kavya:** Mum. You were right. I'm switching it off.
**Mum:** Who are you talking to?

chapters.title: The firm saves you some marks

lines.cap: **Narrator:** Before the credits, the firm would like to save you some marks.
**Constance:** One. Energy is **never created or destroyed**. Not used up. Not lost. **Transferred**.
**Pat:** Two. **Heat, light, sound** and **electricity** are **pathways**, not stores. I'm. Not. A. Store.
**Theo:** Three. Wasted energy **dissipates** into the **thermal store** of the surroundings. Hello again.
**Effie:** Four. Efficiency is **never** more than **100%**. Never. I've checked.
**Colin:** Five. **Nuclear** is **non-renewable**. Uranium runs out. Like me.
**Jules:** Six! Energy is measured in **joules**! Not watts! Not degrees! That's me!
**Narrator:** Every Joule Counts will return.
**Constance:** Gerald. Anything you'd like to add?
**Gerald:** ...Finally!
**Constance:** Gravitational potential, to kinetic. Filed.
**Theo:** And now his joules are in my department.
**Gerald:** Worth it.
